overview.text: The Viperine Snake is a small water snake of south-western Europe and north-western Africa. It spends much of its life in and around rivers, ponds and streams, hunting fish and frogs. Its zigzag pattern, a head that can look triangular and a viper-like defensive display make many people mistake it for a viper - which is how it got its common name - but it has no venom dangerous to people.

identification.text: Grey, brown or reddish above, with a dark zigzag stripe along the middle of the back and a row of dark eye-spots with yellowish centres along each side. Viper-like markings and a head that can look triangular are the reason it is confused with vipers.

size.label: Adults
size.text: A relatively small snake, reaching up to about 80 cm in total length; a typical adult length is not given in SnakeList's sources.

size.label: Males and females
size.text: Females are the larger sex: in studies in Sardinia and in the Ebro Delta (Spain), females were longer than males.

distribution.label: Native
distribution.text: Portugal, Spain (including Gibraltar), France, south-western Switzerland and north-western Italy, plus Sardinia; and in North Africa, Morocco, northern Algeria, Tunisia and north-western Libya.

distribution.label: Central Algeria
distribution.text: A 2024 record from central Algeria extended its known range southwards, into the Sahara.

distribution.label: Introduced
distribution.text: Mallorca and Menorca in the Balearic Islands. A genetic study suggests it reached Mallorca from south-eastern France around Roman times, so it is an ancient introduction rather than a recent one.

habitat.text: Closely tied to fresh water: rivers, streams, ponds, lakes, irrigation channels and other wetlands, where it hunts in the water and basks on the banks.

behaviour.text: When threatened on land it hisses and strikes in a viper-like way, but usually does not actually bite.

diet.text: Mainly fish and amphibians, caught in the water.

diet.label: Young snakes (Ebro Delta, Spain)
diet.text: Juveniles ate a more varied diet than adults, taking many tadpoles and earthworms; adults ate mostly fish. Males took more small carp and large females more frogs.

diet.label: On Mallorca
diet.text: It preys on Perez's Frog, among other animals.

reproduction.text: Lays eggs. In one study, females did not lay bigger or more frequent clutches when food was more plentiful, unlike many other snakes.

conservation.text: Listed as Least Concern globally, although its numbers are reported to be declining.

conservation.label: On Mallorca
conservation.text: Predation by viperine snakes is believed to be one of the causes of the decline of the rare Mallorcan Midwife Toad, and removing snakes has been tried at some toad sites.

similar.text: the other Natrix of Iberia; it has reddish eyes and lacks the Viperine Snake's dark zigzag along the back.
